subject: history
topic: Why the history of 'scientific' racism was funded by commercial interests
angle: While the sources do not specifically mention 'scientific racism' or 'exploitative labor,' they show that business interests have influenced the development of anthropology and shape the production of pharmaceuticals and societal health.
title: The Commercial Shape of Science

hooks.text: Who decided what your medicine does?
You assume science is neutral. It has business interests.
You trust the experts who work for the market.
A researcher signs a contract with a corporation.
Business interests shape the study of humans.

reveal.headline: Commercial interests have shaped anthropology for nearly a century.
reveal.body: Business interests have influenced the development of the field of anthropology. They also shape the types of pharmaceutical effects that are made and remade for society.

explain.headline: The evidence is mixed on specific historical funding.
explain.body: While research shows a link between commercial interests and societal health, there is no data provided on the specific funding of early biological studies for labor exploitation.

matters.headline: That may be why your health is a commodity.
matters.body: If corporations are structural factors in disease and academic researchers serve as suppliers to business, your physical well-being is tied to a commercial cycle.

example.headline: You pick up a bottle of medicine at the pharmacy.
example.body: You look at the label and the price. You assume it is a neutral cure for a physical problem.

question.headline: Who owns the definition of your health?

stat.label: the duration of commercial influence on anthropology

claims.text: Pharmaceuticals are not “discovered”; they are made and remade in relation to shifting contexts.
claims.quote: We show that there is no pure (pharmaceutical) object that precedes its socialization. Pharmaceuticals are not “discovered”; they are made and remade in relation to shifting contexts.

claims.text: Prominent academic researchers may become intellectual “suppliers” to businesses.
claims.quote: Over time, this field has attracted prominent academic researchers (as will be discussed herein), who may become intellectual “suppliers” to businesses, and thus part of the field.

claims.text: Corporations and other commercial interests are a distal, structural, societal factor that causes disease and injury.
claims.quote: we propose a framework to systematically study corporations and other commercial interests as a distal, structural, societal factor that causes disease and injury.

claims.text: The nation-state is complicated by the emergence to dominance of state and state-like oligarchic-corporate state formations.
claims.quote: the political environment of the nation-state is complicated by the emergence to dominance of state and state-like oligarchic-corporate state formations.

claims.text: The field of anthropology has been influenced by the domain of business for the better part of a century.
claims.quote: the expansive domain of business... has influenced the development or “making” of anthropology as a discipline and a profession for the better part of a century

claims.text: Commercial interests and societal concerns shape the kinds of pharmaceutical effects that are actualized.
claims.quote: This literature foregrounds insights into how commercial interests and societal concerns shape the kinds of pharmaceutical effects that are actualized

verdict: The evidence confirms that commercial interests influence anthropological development and pharmaceutical production, but it lacks specific data on the funding of early biological studies for labor exploitation.
caveat: None of the provided sources contain any information regarding the specific history of 'scientific' racism or the history of labor exploitation.
caption:
Commercial interests shape the way we study humans and treat disease.

Research shows that business interests have influenced anthropology for nearly a century and shape pharmaceutical production. However, the evidence does not specifically address the funding of early biological studies for labor exploitation.

How does knowing this change your trust in medical research?
